claim: runs-all.json says 10 generations at 12.07 s for the same run. Which file is right is not settled, so it gets no table row.
found: It is settled by the run's own files: runs/r9-ab-certain-1/run.log ends 'evolve: DONE' and 'exit 0' after 10 generations (start 14:10 ET), and its gpu-profile.json gives a warm (gens 4-9) mean of 12.07 s/gen and a tail share of 56.2%, the same as runs-all.json. The runs.json 'certain' entry (exit null, gens 0) started at 11:58 ET, so it is a crashed attempt from the 11:53 A/B carried under the afternoon name. The post-fix tail,certain run is 12.07 vs default 12.60 s/gen at n = 1 per arm, still unproven, so the row verdict stands.

claim: Wrong-or-missing: r9-ab-default-1 tail share conflict: 42.6% vs 35.2% (evidence-profile).
found: The 42.6% is not r9-ab-default-1's figure. runs.json carries r9pre-ab-default-1's numbers under that name (the report says so for warm s/gen). The run's own gpu-profile.json gives 42.0% (tail bucket / wall over gens 4-9), which matches runs-all.json (ts_r9def_runsall, 0.4197). This is a three-way conflict, 42.0% / 42.6% / 35.2%, and the box quotes the mislabeled value. lit/evidence-profile.json also uses a different definition (share of the launch span) and a warm of 10.91 s/gen that no other file gives for this run.
source: runs/r9-ab-default-1/gpu-profile.json → generations[4:].buckets.tail / wall; runs-all.json → [name=r9-ab-default-1].tailShare; runs.json → ab.default[0].tailShare

claim: Also measured: The afternoon A/B in runs.json, one run per arm, default 12.80 s (r9-ab-default-1), tail 13.89 s (r9-ab-tail-1), n = 1.
found: These are listed as afternoon A/B figures, but the report itself shows they are the 11:53 ET values (r9pre-ab-default-1 = 12.80, r9pre-ab-tail-1 = 13.89; runs.json start 1792252387 = 11:53 ET). The afternoon runs began at 14:05 ET (runs/r9-ab-default-1/run.log wall start). A figure two files disagree on appears here as a plain measurement under the wrong label. Also, n = 1 does not fit: these runs belong to a 3-per-arm A/B.
source: runs.json → ab.default[0].start, ab.tail[0].start; runs-all.json → r9pre-ab-default-1, r9pre-ab-tail-1; runs/r9-ab-default-1/run.log → wall start

claim: Also measured: Occupancy's overnight chain ... 11.61 s (occ-ni-a/b) over n = 2 runs
found: occ/runs.json's warm_s_per_gen_mean is the mean of gens 1-9. The study's warmPerGen, used by every other figure in the report, is the mean of gens 4-9 (from gen 'sat'). On that definition occ-ni-a/b are 11.62 / 11.43, mean 11.52 s/gen (runs-all.json). The figure is shown next to the interleaved numbers on a different definition, and nothing says so.

claim: Tail share is the scorer's tailShare field in runs-all.json, the part of each launch after half its battles have ended.
found: Wrong definition. runs-all.json tailShare is sum(generations[g].buckets.tail) / sum(generations[g].wall) over warm gens 4-9 of gpu-profile.json. Recomputed exactly for all 12 runs in runs/, e.g. ab-base-1 0.4392. It is a share of warm-generation wall, not of launch span. Tail ms / span ms per launch gives 0.4125 for ab-base-1. 'After half its battles have ended' is lit/evidence-profile.json's definition. The figures themselves are correct.

claim: The morning runs were never diffed against default, so the checkpoint diff comes first. / Compact state's checkpoint match rests on its result card.
found: The data holds same-seed evidence the report misses: every per-generation 'done' line (mean fitness, opponent fitness, raw win rates, battle counts) and the final 'Top team' line in ab-stack-1..3/run.log match ab-base-1..3 exactly (identical hash for all 12 runs in runs/). This is not a checkpoint diff, but it supports 'its results match' and should be cited.

claim: decision-table row tail v2: change '9.10 s alone'
found: The Change column holds differences against default in every other row, but this row holds an absolute single-run warm time (9.1 s/gen). Read as a change, it looks like a 9-second effect. ab-tailv2.json's 9.1 / 118.2 are rounded figures with no per-gen walls behind them. The row verdict (unproven) is right.
